entities.summary: Duke Joseph François Louis Charles de Damas was a French general who led the French army to victory in the French Revolutionary Wars. Born on October 28, 1758, in Paris, France, he rose to prominence during the tumultuous years of the French Revolution and the subsequent Napoleonic Wars. De Damas's military career was marked by his bravery and strategic thinking, earning him a reputation as one of the most skilled French generals of his time. He died on March 5, 1829, in Paris, leaving behind a legacy as a military leader who played a significant role in shaping the course of French history. As he reflected on his life, de Damas said, 'A good soldier is always prepared to sacrifice himself for the greater good.' This quote encapsulates his unwavering commitment to duty and country, which defined his life and career. De Damas's impact on French history can be seen in the many battles he fought and won, including the Battle of Valmy, which marked a turning point in the French Revolutionary Wars. His military prowess and leadership skills were widely admired by his contemporaries, and he remains a celebrated figure in French military history.
